title: The Last Wolf Revisited
premise: Mara Almeida, the last swordspeaker, has spent her life in the valley of Vael Hollow, where wards suppress all magic—including her own inherited gift. When the border wards collapse and the stars go dark on the same night, she learns her grandmother's oath bound not just Mara but an entire hidden country that officially ceased to exist a century ago. Guided by a dying dragon's ember and a disgraced cartographer who maps places that no longer are, Mara must find the Door of Return and speak the truth-words that will either restore her nation or dissolve it forever. In the end, Mara chooses to unbind the oath rather than renew it, freeing magic—and herself—at the cost of the valley's invisibility, and becomes the first free wolf in a thousand years.
about_author: Ines Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border treaties between countries that no longer exist. She writes fantasy about inheritance, oaths, and the geography of forgetting from a farmhouse full of unread atlases.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. On the eve of the valley's Quiet Festival, the stars vanish one constellation at a time while Mara practices sword-forms she was forbidden to name aloud. Her grandmother's death-day candle gutters blue. The emotional beat is dread disguised as routine—Mara senses the world holding its breath.

chapters.title: Wards Like Old Scars
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She walks the border stones at dawn and finds them cold for the first time in living memory. The village elder insists nothing has changed; Mara's hands shake anyway. Beat: the loneliness of seeing what others refuse to see.

chapters.title: A Stranger With No Shadow
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A traveler arrives whose shadow lags half a step behind him—Corvin, a cartographer exiled for mapping erased places. He carries a map of Vael Hollow that shows doors where there are only walls. Beat: wary fascination; the first crack in Mara's isolation.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Buried
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Searching her grandmother's locked chest, Mara finds an oath-blade, a wolf-tooth sigil, and a letter beginning 'If you are reading this, the country has begun to die.' Beat: grief curdling into betrayal—her whole life was a hiding place.

chapters.title: The Ember That Would Not Die
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Corvin. Corvin reveals he follows a dragon-ember that burns without fuel, drawing him toward the last living piece of the vanished country of Sarnholt—of which Vael Hollow is the hidden heart. Beat: reluctant alliance sealed over shared exile.

chapters.title: Swordspeaking
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Outside the weakened wards, Mara's blade begins to hum with words she never learned—her inherited gift waking. She accidentally speaks a fence into splinters. Beat: terror and exhilaration entwined; power as inheritance and burden.

chapters.title: The Village Decides
chapters.summary: Multiple POV chapter. The elders vote to seal the valley completely, erasing even memory of the outside. Mara's childhood friend Tamsin betrays her presence to the council out of love. Beat: loyalty pulling against truth, both wearing kind faces.

chapters.title: Flight Across the Gray Fields
chapters.summary: Mara and Corvin's POV, alternating. They flee north through farmland that literally fades behind them—the dying country eating its own edges. Beat: urgency and wonder; the landscape itself is a countdown.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Confession
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Corvin admits his guild sent him to erase the last map of Sarnholt, not save it; he kept one copy instead. Beat: trust nearly shatters, then deepens—two people who chose truth over their orders.

chapters.title: City of the Unremembered
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. They reach a city of people struck from every record, ruled by a librarian-queen who collects names. She recognizes Mara's sigil and demands the oath-blade as toll. Beat: temptation of belonging without freedom.

chapters.title: Names Are Doors
chapters.summary: Librarian-queen's POV. She explains that Sarnholt was unwritten, not destroyed—an entire nation edited out by treaty, its people scattered into forgetting. The Door of Return exists only in the true name of its last heir. Beat: revelation reframing everything Mara thought she knew.

chapters.title: Tamsin at the Gate
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Sent to drag Mara home, Tamsin instead finds the gray fields swallowing the valley's outskirts. She chooses to warn Mara rather than capture her. Beat: loyalty transformed—love means telling hard truths.

chapters.title: The Dragon's Last Fire
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Following the ember to its source, they find Ashvane, a dragon reduced to a coal-sized flame in a shrine of ash, keeper of the Door. He offers passage but warns: opening the door restores Sarnholt AND rebinds every descendant to the old oath. Beat: the cost made explicit.

chapters.title: The Oath's True Wording
chapters.summary: Ashvane's POV, ancient memory. Flashback to the original binding: the first wolves swore themselves as the country's walls, trading freedom for protection. Mara realizes her 'gift' is a leash. Beat: horror of inheritance; identity as something imposed.

chapters.title: Hunters of the Treaty
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Enforcers of the old treaty arrive to extinguish Ashvane and kill the last heir. A running battle through the shrine; Corvin is gravely wounded shielding the map. Beat: stakes turn mortal; no more retreat.

chapters.title: What I Am Not
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, quiet interlude. Keeping vigil over Corvin, Mara interrogates who she'd be without the oath, the valley, the title of last anything. Beat: the still center before the storm; identity chosen rather than assigned.

chapters.title: The Door of Return
chapters.summary: Mara, Corvin, and Tamsin's POV braided. They reach the Door—a seam of starlight in a hillside that shouldn't exist. It opens only to the oath spoken willingly. Beat: threshold awe; the past waiting to be answered.

chapters.title: The Words I Was Never Taught
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Inside the threshold, Mara faces the echo of the first wolf, who tests her with the life she could have had—a safe, warded, small forever. Beat: climax of identity; she refuses the false comfort.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At the Door, Mara speaks new words: not renewal but release, dissolving the oath and returning Sarnholt to the world as memory and choice rather than law. Ashvane spends his last fire to hold the door open. Beat: climax—sacrifice, agency, irreversible change.

chapters.title: After the Stars Return
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Stars reignite; the gray fields bloom back into named land; the valley's wards fall gently, like snow. Some villagers grieve their invisibility; others walk out weeping with joy. Beat: bittersweet dawn; freedom is disorienting.

chapters.title: The First Free Wolf
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara buries the oath-blade and plants a tree over it, keeping the sword-forms as dance rather than duty. Corvin begins mapping the restored country; Tasmis founds its first archive. Beat: resolution—inheritance transformed into gift.

chapters.title: Revisited
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, epilogue. Years later, travelers come to Vael Hollow asking about the last swordspeaker, and Mara tells them the truth: there was no last one, because there will be more. Beat: peace earned; the story ends where identity begins—chosen, spoken, shared.
